comparison: Perfect agreement on negative feedback loop claims (C4, C43-C45, C84). Both evaluations recognize this as an important finding showing EIN3 binding to and regulating negative regulators of ethylene signaling. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as a key contribution without raising concerns.

Disagreement on transcription factor motif analysis (C66-C68). OpenEval finds the PBM data and motif enrichment analysis statistically compelling. Peer reviewers accept the approach as 'clever' but express uncertainty about whether temporal wave dynamics were adequately considered in the analysis, requesting clarification on wave-specific effects.

Agreement on conservation and broader significance claims (C86-C89). Both evaluations accept the evidence for EIN3 conservation across plant lineages and the broader implications for understanding ethylene signaling. Peer reviewers implicitly support these conclusions through their overall positive assessment of the work's significance.

Partial disagreement on ARF transcription factor findings (C70-C79, C94-C96). OpenEval finds comprehensive support from ChIP-Seq, expression, phylogenetic, and genetic data. Peer reviewers accept the general findings ('nicely demonstrated') but request additional experiments on transcript levels in double mutants and functional rescue experiments, indicating the evidence is incomplete for full support of functional claims.

Agreement on hormone pathway cross-regulation (C5, C40, C46-C51, C83 overlap with broader R4 claims). Both evaluations recognize this as an important finding. OpenEval emphasizes the statistical strength (p=10⁻⁹⁶) and network analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the hormone cross-talk findings without raising concerns.

Significant disagreement on temporal wave identification (C3, C22-C24, C29-C30, C33-C34). OpenEval finds strong statistical support (DREM p<10⁻¹⁰) for coordinated waves. Peer reviewers acknowledge waves as 'important' but express specific concern about Wave 1, noting genes 'appear to move in opposite fashion at different time points' and requesting clarification or cluster refinement.

Agreement on ChIP-Seq and mRNA-Seq integration (C20, C103 overlap). OpenEval supports the finding that binding doesn't quantitatively predict transcription. Peer reviewers praise the 'coordinated analysis' and note the integration 'greatly increases the inferences that can be drawn,' though they raise nomenclature concerns about defining 'targets' that don't challenge the underlying data.

Agreement on EIN3 as transcriptional activator (C14-C15 overlap). OpenEval finds support from quantitative mRNA-Seq and GO enrichment. Peer reviewers' praise of the integrated analysis implicitly accepts these findings, though their nomenclature concern about 'targets' relates to how regulated genes are classified.

Agreement on jasmonate pathway regulation (C52-C53, C55 overlap). OpenEval supports the anticipatory binding model based on ChIP-Seq and mRNA-Seq data. Peer reviewers accept hormone cross-talk findings broadly, which encompasses the jasmonate interactions, without raising specific concerns about these claims.

Agreement on gibberellin pathway regulation (C57-C58 overlap). OpenEval finds support from ChIP-Seq binding data and motif enrichment. Peer reviewers' acceptance of hormone cross-talk findings includes gibberellin interactions, with no specific concerns raised about these claims.

Agreement on auxin pathway regulation (C61-C62 overlap). OpenEval supports claims with ChIP-Seq and mRNA-Seq data, appropriately qualifying tissue-specificity speculation. Peer reviewers accept hormone cross-talk findings broadly, which includes auxin pathway interactions.

OpenEval identifies speculative mechanistic claims (C32, C35-C39, C64) about wave characteristics and desensitization as uncertain, requiring additional experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative interpretations.

OpenEval categorizes extensive background literature claims (C1-C2, C6-C11, C19, C31, C41-C42, C44-C45, C54, C56, C60, C63, C65, C69, C78, C80-C81, C85) as supported by prior work. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual claims from the literature.

OpenEval supports basic quantitative results from differential expression analysis (C13, C102) showing minimal overlap between induced and repressed genes. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these specific quantitative findings.
OpenEval supports methodological descriptions and basic dataset characterization (C90-C91, C97, C101). No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these methodological and descriptive claims.

OpenEval supports ChIP-Seq quantitative results (C92-C93, C99) including recovery of known targets and promoter enrichment. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these validation metrics.
